clue.text: Where it's residential as far as outskirts of Washington?

parts.note: 'up to' means as far as, as in 'up to the river'

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its outermost letters, first and last

explanation.surface: A query about where homes start when heading out toward the edges of the American capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of' takes W and N, the ends of Washington.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage the uptown part of a city is typically its residential district, away from the business centre.

clue.text: Disconnected a French editor packing punch

indicators.note: packing means holding something inside, so the French article and editor together enclose the punch

parts.note: un is the French for a
a hook is a boxing punch thrown with a bent arm

explanation.surface: A Parisian editor carrying a punch, perhaps in both senses, was cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking something off its fastening detaches or disconnects it, as with a trailer.

clue.text: Toddler in shade clutching new toy

indicators.note: one word clutching another grips it inside

parts.note: a tint is a shade of colour

indicators.note: new means the letters come in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A small child playing in the shade hugs a new plaything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shade' suggests shadow, but here it is a hue of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A very small child just learning to walk is affectionately called this.

clue.text: Percussion instrument was hard to get on table

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
a board is a table, as in 'board and lodging' or a festive board

explanation.surface: Someone found it difficult to put a drum on the table.
explanation.definitionFit: The ridged laundry board was played with thimbles in skiffle and jug bands as a rhythm instrument.

clue.text: Poem also written about storm

indicators.note: one word written about another is set around it, enclosing it

parts.note: 'then' can mean also or besides, as in 'and then there's the cost'
to rave is to storm or rage

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a poem was additionally composed concerning a tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Allan Poe's famous narrative poem, with its refrain 'Nevermore', bears this title.

clue.text: Helps her putt in tight game

indicators.note: tight in its slang sense of drunk signals the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A golfing scene: a partner helps a woman sink a putt in a close match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' means drunk, so HELPS HER PUTT IN is scrambled. The game is a parlour game: players in a circle pass a shoe secretly while one in the middle tries to find it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a traditional children's party game, a specific example of a game.

clue.text: Bird, black and gold, rising over one end of garden

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
or is gold in heraldry
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A dark and golden bird flies up from the far end of a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns B OR into ROB; 'end of' gives N from garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-breasted garden songbird is a familiar British species.

clue.text: Opinion of composer, extremely coherent

parts.note: Giuseppe Verdi was the Italian opera composer

indicators.note: extremely means taking the extreme letters, first and last

explanation.surface: A critic's view of Verdi as being thoroughly lucid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes C and T, the ends of coherent.
explanation.definitionFit: A judgement or considered view, as in 'what's your view on it?'

clue.text: Spice in overturned stone cask

indicators.note: overturned in a down clue means the whole is turned upside down, read from the bottom

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone
a tun is a large beer or wine cask

explanation.surface: A spice is found inside a stone barrel that has toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns GEM TUN into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The aromatic seed of an Indonesian tree is ground for use as a seasoning.

clue.text: Getting on coach for Greyfriars, say

parts.note: boarding a vehicle is getting on it
to school someone is to coach or train them

explanation.surface: Pupils climbing aboard a bus for an outing to a Franciscan priory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' looks like a bus but is the verb to train. Greyfriars is the fictional residential school of the Billy Bunter stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Greyfriars is an example of a school where pupils live during term.

clue.text: Factory workers not working with complete ease

parts.note: manual workers are called hands, as in factory hands
a system that is down is not working

explanation.surface: Mill staff on strike, perhaps, though the phrase pretends to describe them idling comfortably.
explanation.definitionFit: To win by this idiom is to win effortlessly, from jockeys easing off with hands lowered.

clue.text: Pop first of balloons, upsetting relative's son terribly

indicators.note: 'first of' applies to every following word, taking the opening letter of each in turn

explanation.surface: Popping a child's balloons dreadfully upsets a cousin's boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of' reaches past balloons to all five words, giving B, U, R, S, T; 'upsetting' looks like an anagram signal but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To pop a balloon is to make it rupture with a bang, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Oscar has to be in credit for a month

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: 'in' says the words to be go inside the abbreviation for credit

parts.note: CR is the standard abbreviation for credit in accounts

explanation.surface: An Academy Award winner is due to be in the black for a month.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenth month of the calendar year is a particular example of a month.

clue.text: Tenor keeping money for annuity scheme

indicators.note: one word keeping another holds it inside itself

parts.note: tenor in the sense of general drift or character means tone, as in 'the tone of the meeting'
tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: A singer holds on to cash to fund a pension plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tenor' suggests the abbreviation T, but here it means the drift or tone of something.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an investment scheme in which subscribers share an annuity, survivors' shares growing as members die.

clue.text: Spare more

definitions.meaning: a spare item is an additional one held in reserve
'more' as in an added amount, beyond what is usual

explanation.definitionFit: An additional item is both a spare and something more than the usual amount.

clue.text: At work, actor's union reveals unfairness

parts.note: someone at work is in, as in 'is the boss in today?'
Equity is the British trade union for actors and performers

explanation.surface: A performers' trade union exposes injustice in the workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: Injustice or lack of fairness is the sense; equity means fairness, and the prefix negates it.

clue.text: Runs a live broadcast, worldwide

indicators.note: broadcast in its sense of scattered widely signals a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A network airs a live programme to a global audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' scatters the letters of RUNS A LIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something applying everywhere or to all is global in reach.

clue.text: Stand at Leeds ground under roof of pavilion

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts the second piece below the first
in a down clue the roof of a word is its top, its opening letter
ground as the past tense of grind means crushed and remade, so the letters rearrange

explanation.surface: A cricket spectator's seat at the Leeds ground below the pavilion roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roof of' gives P; 'ground' rearranges AT LEEDS, which sits 'under' it. Headingley in Leeds is a Test cricket ground with a pavilion.
explanation.definitionFit: A base or plinth on which a statue rests is a stand of this kind.

clue.text: Ordered gold pair — that may be recklessly extravagant

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order, rearranged

explanation.surface: A spendthrift has ordered a matching couple of gold items.
explanation.definitionFit: As in the parable of the son who squandered his inheritance, the word means wastefully lavish.

clue.text: Cloth figure dog chewed during most of mass meeting

indicators.note: during says one piece is set within the other
most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a rally is a mass meeting

indicators.note: chewed means mangled, so the letters rearrange

explanation.surface: At a big gathering a dog chews up a soft toy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cloth figure' could suggest a number in a fabric sale; it is a soft toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A floppy toy figure made of fabric and stuffing, such as a child's doll.

clue.text: Question children

definitions.meaning: a question in the sense of a matter under debate, a point at stake
a legal and formal word for offspring, as in 'died without'

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a disputed point and one's offspring, as in 'without male heirs'.

clue.text: Stun gun initially held by old actor

indicators.note: one piece held by another sits inside it

parts.note: an old stager is a veteran, originally an experienced actor

indicators.note: initially means the first letter

explanation.surface: A veteran performer's weapon is used to shock someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives G from gun, 'held by' STAGER.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish or amaze someone is to stun them, as with news that bowls one over.

clue.text: Run-down saloon perhaps causing bishop great displeasure

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
anger is strong displeasure

explanation.surface: A clapped-out car annoys the bishop who owns it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saloon' is a car, not a bar. Banger is British slang for an old, battered car.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilapidated old car, of which a saloon is one kind, is called this in British slang.

clue.text: Cake decoration, almost heavenly

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: angelica is candied green plant stem used to decorate cakes

explanation.surface: A cake topping looks nearly divine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final A of ANGELICA.
explanation.definitionFit: Being like the celestial messengers of God, it means divine or heavenly.

clue.text: Relish circuit before winning

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a track
up means ahead, winning, as in 'two goals up'

explanation.surface: A racer savours a lap of the track while leading.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept eagerly or enjoy is to relish, like a cat lapping milk.

clue.text: Quietly tell ecclesiastical dignitary

parts.note: P is piano, quietly, in musical notation
to relate a story is to tell it

explanation.surface: An instruction to whisper something to a senior churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop or other high-ranking churchman is called by this title.

clue.text: Team climb round face of Rushmore

indicators.note: the phrase for climbing goes round, enclosing, the other letter

parts.note: to climb is to go up

indicators.note: the face of a word is its front, its opening letter

explanation.surface: A team scales the sculpted face of Mount Rushmore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face of' gives R from Rushmore, which 'round' places inside GO UP.
explanation.definitionFit: A team is a set of people working together, a band or collective.

clue.text: Inadvertent mistake concerning vision

parts.note: over can mean concerning, as in 'a dispute over money'
sight is the faculty of vision

explanation.surface: A careless slip relating to someone's eyesight.
explanation.definitionFit: An unintentional failure to notice something is a slip of this kind.

clue.text: Plump for pudding

definitions.meaning: a British steamed or baked pudding of suet pastry rolled up with jam

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a chubby person and also a rolled jam suet pudding, a British school-dinner classic.

clue.text: More than one chum swallowing bait, briefly

indicators.note: one word swallowing another takes it inside

parts.note: a pal is a chum, a friend

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a lure is bait used to attract fish

explanation.surface: An angling picture: a friend's catch swallowing bait quickly, more than one fish.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar this form indicates several items rather than a single one.
